description:
FILED s514d (Opus, 2026-10-10) while writing Pl/t/tiehandle-01.t: the TRANSPILER HANGS (100 % CPU, no output, never returns) on a double-quoted string that interpolates `$\` followed by an escaped backslash.

Reproducer (perl 5.40.3 prints `ors=Z\|` then `Z`; `./pl2cl` never finishes -- `timeout 10 ./pl2cl h2.pl` exits 124):

    local $\ = "Z"; my $s = "ors=$\\"; print STDOUT $s, "|\n";

An ALRM handler with Carp::confess never fires, so the time is spent inside ONE regex match (perl defers safe signals during a regex op): a catastrophic-backtracking or self-looping pattern somewhere in the interpolation scan of `$\` (Pl/InterpScan.pm is the one scanner, standing rule §8).  Not caused by s514d (no Pl/ change in member 1); the guard row was rewritten as `"..." . $\` to keep it out of the way.

Rule 12 / #138 family: a hang is worse than a die -- a whole program never transpiles and the sweep / everyday see a TIMEOUT.
subject: pl2cl HANGS (one regex never returns) on "...$\\" -- a $\ interpolation followed by an escaped backslash
